ai.title: Add keep to placeholder comment regex in common/src/util/string.ts
ai.summary: The `replaceNonStandardPlaceholderComments` function now matches `keep` in its regex patterns. Previously, comments using `keep` (e.g., `// ... keep ...`) were ignored. This change ensures they are normalized to `... existing code ...`. The update applies to all supported comment styles (C, Python, HTML, SQL, MATLAB) in `common/src/util/string.ts`.

eli5.text: When the tool writes sample code with holes in it (the 'keep writing here' kind of comment), it already turned a few common phrases into the same placeholder. Now it also recognizes the word 'keep' in those comments, no matter what language the code is written in. If you look at generated snippets, comments that say something like '... keep...' will appear as '... existing code...' instead of being left as-is. It's already live and applies to all the programming languages the placeholder feature supports.

ai.title: Add --auto-git flag to stage changes before applying
ai.summary: CLI adds `--auto-git` flag. `stageAllChanges` runs `git add .` via `execSync` before `applyChanges` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Argument parsing shifts to `process.argv.slice(2)` in `npm-app/src/index.ts` to extract flag, stripping it before passing `projectPath` and `initialInput`. `npm-app/package.json` `start` script enables flag by default.

eli5.text: When you run the tool with the new --auto-git option, it now stages your work automatically using git before applying any new changes, and it tells you in green text that your previous changes have been saved. This flag is turned on by default when starting the tool, but it currently only handles staging; it does not commit or push the staged changes for you. If you look at how the tool starts, you would see it passes --auto-git to the command, and you would see a green line in the console confirming your work is staged.

ai.title: Make second ellipsis optional in placeholder comment regexes
ai.summary: Updated regexes in common/src/util/string.ts to make the trailing ellipsis optional in non-standard placeholder comment detection. This ensures comments like `// ... existing code` without a second `...` are correctly normalized to `// ... existing code ...`. Affects C-style, Python, HTML, SQL, and MATLAB comment patterns.

eli5.text: When the assistant finds a shortened note in your code that means 'leave the existing code here,' it now treats a missing second set of dots as the same kind of note. For example, a note written as `//... rest of code` without a trailing `...` is now filled in to look like `//... existing code...`, matching the way it handles notes that do include the second set of dots. This affects every style of comment the assistant recognizes, including those used in JavaScript, Python, SQL, and MATLAB files, so mixed formats are normalized consistently. The change is live today.

ai.title: /usage command and credits in response-complete
ai.summary: Added `usage` and `credits` aliases to the CLI, triggering a new `usage` websocket action that returns a `usage-response` payload. The `response-complete` server action now embeds `usage` and `limit` fields, allowing the client to store them and display a warning via `showUsageWarning` without a separate websocket round-trip. The `sendUsageUpdate` helper was refactored into `calculateUsage`, and the server action type `usage` was renamed to `usage-response` to avoid collision with the new client action.

eli5.text: You can now type "usage" or "credits" in the command line to see how many credits you have left before hitting your limit. After the assistant finishes editing your file, it also shows you a warning directly in the response (like "You have used 75% of your monthly usage limit") instead of making a separate request behind the scenes. Both the new command and the on-screen warning pull from the same real-time credit count, so the number you see is always current.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.82
ai.summary: Internal version increment to 1.0.82. Updates npm-app/package.json. No user-facing changes or new features.

eli5.text: The app's internal tracking number was bumped up to the next build, which bundles together several improvements that rolled in over the previous day. Most of what you'd see is that logs coming from inside the app now follow a cleaner, more standardized format, the AI helper is better at recognizing and fixing up oddly formatted code comments, and two new behind-the-scenes tools are available: one lets the AI automatically prepare changes for saving, and another gives you a way to check your usage and credits via a simple command. None of this adds a brand-new feature you'd click on, but it smooths out how the app keeps itself tidy and reports its work.

ai.title: Pricing page redirects unauthenticated users to login
ai.summary: Pricing page now checks session status before creating Stripe checkout session. Unauthenticated users redirect to /login instead of proceeding. Change affects web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx. Uses next/navigation router.push for redirect.

eli5.text: When you click the upgrade button on the pricing page, the site now checks whether you're signed in first. If you're not logged in, it sends you to the login screen instead of moving forward with payment. You'd notice this if you tried to sign up for the Pro plan without an account: you'd be redirected to sign in before you could proceed. This started working today.

ai.title: Update Pro pricing page credits and features
ai.summary: Pro tier credits set to literal 10_000 instead of CREDITS_USAGE_LIMITS.PAID. Added overage allowance feature text ($0.50 per 100 credits). Scope limited to web/src/app/pricing/page.tsx. No logic changes, only display data.

eli5.text: The pricing page for the paid Pro plan now shows a fixed 10,000 credits instead of a technical reference, and it adds a new line about paying 50 cents for every extra 100 credits you use. This is purely how the information is displayed, so if you're on the Pro plan or looking at the pricing page, you'll see the updated wording and the new overage detail, but nothing about what you can actually do has changed.

ai.title: Broaden npm detection in update-manicode
ai.summary: detectInstaller in npm-app/src/update-manicode.ts now returns 'npm' when pathIncludesNodeModules, path.includes('npm'), path.startsWith('/usr/'), or npm_config_user_agent includes 'npm'. Previous logic required pathIncludesNodeModules AND (npm or /usr/), missing global installs without node_modules in path. Scope limited to CLI update mechanism. User-agent check adds fallback for npm-managed binaries outside standard paths.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant's command-line tool and it needs to update itself using npm, the tool now recognizes more situations where npm was the one that installed it. Previously, it would only detect npm when the installation path contained 'node_modules' and also mentioned 'npm' or started with '/usr/'; now it also recognizes installations where the path simply includes 'npm', starts with '/usr/', or when the system's user-agent string mentions 'npm', which helps catch globally installed versions that don't show up in the usual paths. This change is live today and only affects the behind-the-scenes self-update mechanism for npm-based installations.
